Seminar Title:

Formulation and Characterization of a Synbiotic Coffee-Chicory Edible Film

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Biotechnology and Medical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Rinita Jonellia A

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

BM Seminar Hall (BM-140)

Date and Time:

10 Nov 2026 10:30 AM

Contact:

Dr. Prasoon Kumar

Abstract:

The growing consumer demand for functional foods that combine sensory appeal, portability, and health promoting properties has driven interest in novel probiotic delivery systems beyond conventional dairy matrices. Coffee is one of the most widely consumed drinks globally for its diverse range of bioactive compounds and chicory in coffee blends enhances sensory characteristics of beverage. This study aimed to develop and optimize a probiotic coffee-chicory edible film fermented with Lactobacillus as functional food. The edible film was formulated to maximize polyphenol content, probiotic stability. The ratio of coffee to chicory was fixed at 70:30 to extract maximum polyphenols. The extract was subsequently fermented with Lactobacillus fermentum strain. The fermented extract was mixed with glycerol and agar-agar and casted as thin films. Results demonstrated that ultrasound assisted extraction significantly improved polyphenol recovery by two fold. The fermentation enhanced antioxidant activity to 56.84% through phenolic biotransformation, and that controlled refrigerated drying preserved probiotic viability above the RDA limits (≥10⁶ CFU/g) in the film, with acceptable mechanical integrity and disintegration time for oral consumption. This work establishes a coffee-chicory based, non-dairy, low moisture, portable synbiotic film as a viable alternative to conventional dairy-based products.
